It went red too with NightWaivers.IssuanceCutOff printed March 15, 2021 (`new(2021, 3, 15)` for `new(2021, 3, 16)`), which released only the case issued on 2021-03-15 -- `Failed:     1, Passed:     3` -- so the just-below-the-cut-off boundary is asserted distinctly, and with NightWaiverTerminationFinding.Authority citing night-operation's `§ 107.29(a)` (`MapEntries.NightOperation.Locator` for `MapEntries.NightWaiverTermination.Locator`) -- `Failed:     4, Passed:     0`. Citing night-waiver-bar's locator did NOT turn it red: the map gives both entries `§ 107.29(d)`, the paragraph's two sentences, so the locator cannot tell them apart and nothing in this engine's output can.

NightWaivers.Termination read the issuance cut-off as inclusive (`certificate.IssuedOn <= IssuanceCutOff` for `<`), so a certificate issued ON March 16, 2021 -- not "prior to" it -- was reported terminated; this test went red -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:     6, Skipped:     0, Total:     7`. Only the at-the-boundary case moved, which is what the boundary case is for; the 2021-04-21 and 2021-05-17 issuance dates in this theory stayed green throughout, so this sentence is never made to reach night-waiver-bar's April 21, 2021 cut-off.

NightWaivers.Termination dropped the conjunct for what the certificate authorizes (`certificate.IssuedOn < IssuanceCutOff` for `certificate.AuthorizesDeviationFromSection10729 && certificate.IssuedOn < IssuanceCutOff`), so a certificate that does not authorize deviation from § 107.29 was terminated on its issuance date alone; this test went red -- `Failed!  - Failed:     2, Passed:     2, Skipped:     0, Total:     4` (the two early issuance dates; the two on or after the cut-off are not reached either way).

NightWaiverTerminationFinding.HasTerminated excluded the termination date itself (`AsOf > NightWaivers.TerminationDate` for `>=`), so asked as of May 17, 2021 -- the date the sentence says the certificates terminate on -- the engine answered that it had not terminated; this test went red -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:     4, Skipped:     0, Total:     5`. Exactly the at-the-date case moved: 2021-05-16 and 2021-05-18 stayed green, so the boundary is pinned at the date and not near it.

NightWaivers.Termination rebuilt the certificate instead of recording the caller's (`new WaiverCertificate(certificate.IssuedOn, certificate.AuthorizesDeviationFromSection10729, certificate.StatedBy)` for `certificate`), so the finding carried an equal certificate that was not the one stated; this test went red -- `Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:     0, Skipped:     0, Total:     1` -- on Assert.Same. Attribution that is reconstructed is not attribution (rules-factory decision 0021).

The wall-clock form of the same default, `request.AsOf ?? DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today)`, never reaches a test run: it fails the build on both target frameworks with `error RK0002: 'DateTime.Today' reads an ambient clock; pass the instant in as an argument instead`. Both are recorded because this is the entry whose dates most invite a clock, and the map is explicit that they are ordinary operations over a date the caller supplies.
